question:
On a checkerboard composed of \(64\) unit squares, what is the probability that a randomly chosen unit square does not touch the outer edge of the board?

[Figure 1](figures/2009_AMC_8_Q10_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The checkerboard has \(8\) rows and \(8\) columns. A square avoids the outer edge exactly when it lies outside the first and last rows and outside the first and last columns.

Removing those rows and columns leaves \(8-2=6\) rows, each containing \(6\) eligible squares. Therefore there are \(6\times6=36\) eligible squares. All \(64\) unit squares are equally likely to be chosen, so the probability is
\[
\frac{36}{64}=\boxed{\frac{9}{16}},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{D}\).

edges.reason: The criteria expressly find common factors and reduce until numerator and denominator are coprime. These are the common-factor contents of the endpoint; finding the greatest factor in a single step is only a shortcut and is outside this required scope.
edges.scope: Finding a shared divisor and recognizing the absence of a shared divisor above one when reducing to simplest form

edges.reason: Reduction replaces numerator and denominator by division by the same common factor, using the value-preserving fraction property.
edges.scope: dividing numerator and denominator by a common number
